# @webwriter/widget

A widget can use a native custom element. The optional `@webwriter/widget` package adds the shared runtime for observing the authored DOM and participating in live sessions.

## `withWidgetRuntime(Base)`

Apply the mixin to your element class before registration. It adds `widgetRuntime` and observes the host attributes listed in `static widgetAttributes`.

```js
import {withWidgetRuntime} from "@webwriter/widget"

class WwLabel extends withWidgetRuntime(HTMLElement) {
  static widgetAttributes = ["label"]

  #label = document.createElement("span")
  #unsubscribe

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).append(document.createElement("slot"), this.#label)
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    super.connectedCallback()
    const {getSnapshot, subscribe} = this.widgetRuntime
    const render = () => { this.#label.textContent = getSnapshot().attributes.label ?? "" }
    this.#unsubscribe = subscribe(render)
    render()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#unsubscribe?.()
    super.disconnectedCallback()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-label", WwLabel)
```

## Modules

For HTML and JavaScript previews, import `renderSandbox` from `@webwriter/widget/sandbox`. This helper creates a self-contained iframe document in an opaque script sandbox, without a server or editor runtime dependency. See [Run HTML in an isolated preview](../domeditor/docs/widgets/guides/libraries.md#run-html-in-an-isolated-preview) for CSP authorization, standalone exports, and supported execution behavior.

A [module](#module-declarations) is a class with the suffix `Core`. Import each module from its own path, such as `@webwriter/widget/drag`. Create the module for the host. Call `connect()` and `disconnect()` in the lifecycle callbacks. Call `refresh()` after the widget changes its shadow DOM. Read the state with `getSnapshot()` and follow it with `subscribe()`, which returns the function that stops following. Pass `rendered` to a core when the widget renders asynchronously. The function returns a promise that settles after the next render. Pass `root` when the shadow root is not `host.shadowRoot`.

| Module | Import path | Core |
|---|---|---|
| [Permissions](#permissions) | `@webwriter/widget/permissions` | `PermissionsCore` |
| [Settings](#settings) | `@webwriter/widget/settings` | `SettingsCore` |
| [Shortcuts](#shortcuts) | `@webwriter/widget/shortcuts` | `ShortcutsCore` |
| [Drag](#drag) | `@webwriter/widget/drag` | `DragCore` |
| [Viewport](#viewport) | `@webwriter/widget/viewport` | `ViewportCore` |
| [Help](#help) | `@webwriter/widget/help` | `HelpCore` |
| [Print note](#print-note) | `@webwriter/widget/print` | `PrintNoteCore`, `documentAddress` |
| [Scene](#scene) | `@webwriter/widget/scene` | `SceneCore`, `sceneElements` |
| [Playback](#playback) | `@webwriter/widget/playback` | `PlaybackCore` |
| [Data block](#data-block-jsondata) | `@webwriter/widget/data` | `JsonDataCore` |
| [Localization](#localization-localizer-widgetmsg) | `@webwriter/widget/localize` | `LocalizeCore` |
| [Exercise](#exercise) | `@webwriter/widget/exercise` | `ExerciseCore` |
| [Helpers](#helpers-transaction-and-whilevisible) | `@webwriter/widget/transaction`, `@webwriter/widget/visible` | `transaction`, `whileVisible` |

A core that depends on another takes it as an option. Pass the `ViewportCore` as `viewport` to `DragCore` for a target in world coordinates, and to `SceneCore` for a scene that is the window of a canvas viewport. The text of `static options`, `static actions`, `static optionGroups`, and `static permissions`, and their `hidden`, `disabled`, and `readOnly` fields, may be a function of the widget. A plain element answers such texts in its own getter with `resolveDeclarations(this, map)` from `@webwriter/widget`.

The examples show the three most used modules. Permissions hides a control and gates an interaction.

```js
import {PermissionsCore} from "@webwriter/widget/permissions"

class WwHintCard extends HTMLElement {
  static permissions = {
    allowHint: {label: {_: "Learners may reveal the hint in this widget"}, attribute: "allow-hint"},
  }

  #permissions = new PermissionsCore(this)

  constructor() {
    super()
    const root = this.attachShadow({mode: "open"})
    root.innerHTML = `
      <slot></slot>
      <div data-ww-can="allowHint">
        <button>Hint</button>
        <div id="hint" hidden><slot name="hint"></slot></div>
      </div>
    `
    const hint = root.getElementById("hint")
    root.querySelector("button").addEventListener("click", () => (hint.hidden = !hint.hidden))
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#permissions.connect()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#permissions.disconnect()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-hint-card", WwHintCard)
```

Settings stores each setting as an attribute and binds the controls marked `data-ww-setting`. `defineProperties()` gives the host one property per setting.

```js
import {SettingsCore} from "@webwriter/widget/settings"

class WwSimulation extends HTMLElement {
  static settings = {
    population: {type: Number, default: 200, min: 10, max: 2000, step: 10, label: {_: "Population"}},
    showChart: {type: Boolean, default: true, label: {_: "Show chart"}},
  }

  #settings = new SettingsCore(this)
  #unsubscribe

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `
      <p></p>
      <label><span data-ww-setting-label="population"></span> <input type="number" data-ww-setting="population"></label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" data-ww-setting="showChart"> Chart</label>
    `
    this.#settings.defineProperties()
  }

  get options() {
    return this.#settings.editorOptions()
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#settings.connect()
    this.#unsubscribe = this.#settings.subscribe(() => this.#render())
    this.#render()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#unsubscribe?.()
    this.#settings.disconnect()
  }

  #render() {
    const chart = this.#settings.get("showChart") ? ", with chart" : ""
    this.shadowRoot.querySelector("p").textContent = `${this.#settings.get("population")} people${chart}`
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-simulation", WwSimulation)
```

Drag moves authored children. A move changes the authored DOM, so `can` decides who may do it.

```js
import {DragCore} from "@webwriter/widget/drag"
import {PermissionsCore} from "@webwriter/widget/permissions"

class WwSortList extends HTMLElement {
  static permissions = {
    allowReordering: {label: {_: "Learners may reorder the items"}, attribute: "allow-reordering"},
  }

  #permissions = new PermissionsCore(this)
  #drag = new DragCore(this, {can: () => this.#permissions.can("allowReordering")})

  constructor() {
    super()
    const root = this.attachShadow({mode: "open"})
    root.innerHTML = `
      <div data-ww-drop="item" data-ww-drop-position="index">
        <slot data-ww-drag="item" data-ww-drag-via="pointer keyboard"></slot>
      </div>
      <output></output>
    `
    let moves = 0
    root.addEventListener("ww-dragcommit", () => (root.querySelector("output").textContent = `${++moves} moves`))
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#permissions.connect()
    this.#drag.connect()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#drag.disconnect()
    this.#permissions.disconnect()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-sort-list", WwSortList)
```

[Module declarations](#module-declarations) has an example of each other module.

## Shared widget state

The snapshot describes the current DOM. Use attribute names in `static widgetAttributes` and read their values from `attributes`. Values are strings or `null` when an attribute is absent. Set an authored attribute on the host to persist a setting in the document.

| Snapshot fields | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `editable`, `lang`, `standalone` | The host's editing mode, effective language, and standalone attribute. |
| `attributes` | The values for the attributes listed in `static widgetAttributes`. |
| `data`, `dataType`, `dataBlock`, `dataSlot` | The current inert data block and its text, type, and slot. |
| `dataMode` | The current scope. One of `individual`, `all`, `group`, or `local`. |
| `dataReady`, `dataError` | Whether the data scope accepts writes, and the latest error if present. |

Use `host.widgetRuntime.setData(type, text, attrs?)` to write to the data block from an interaction. It updates an existing block in place and rejects writes while a managed scope is pending. For live-session data, use a direct JSON or XML script with `slot="data"` and set `sharedData: true` in the editing configuration. Standalone documents can use the same block as local data. [Data and events](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/data.md)

Put `static options`, `static optionGroups`, `static actions`, and their handler methods on the custom element. WebWriter uses these declarations in the Widget drawer. The runtime and adapters export the corresponding TypeScript declaration types. [Options and actions](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/options-actions.md)

Declare conversions in `static convertFrom` and `static convertTo`. A key that starts with a dot or holds a slash names a file format; every other key is the lowercase tag of an HTML element. Type the maps with `ConvertFromDeclarations` and `ConvertToDeclarations` from `@webwriter/widget`, which every library re-exports, as in `static convertFrom = {ul: "loadList", ".json": "importJson"} satisfies ConvertFromDeclarations`. [Conversions](../domeditor/docs/widgets/guides/conversions.md)

A custom element publishes signals in its `signals` object and receives them through `static effects`, and `static signals` declares the value shape of each published signal. Every library re-exports the shape types and guards of `@webwriter/widget`, such as `isTable`. A widget without Lit imports `signal`, `computed` and `watchSignal` from `@webwriter/widget/signals`. [Make data reactive](../domeditor/docs/widgets/guides/reactivity.md)

## Module declarations

A module supplies one common widget behavior. A widget bundles only the modules that it imports. Mark elements in the shadow root with `data-ww-*` attributes and listen for the module's `ww-*` events. The module handles pointer, touch, and keyboard input. It also handles announcements and cleanup. The sections below name each module's core and declarations. [`@webwriter/lit`](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#modules) describes every module in full, with its options, events, and rules. The rules hold for every library.

A binding of a library has the same name as the module on its own path, such as `@webwriter/react/drag`. The core is the class of `@webwriter/widget`, which a widget can also use directly. The examples in this section are plain custom elements on the cores. Each library's **Modules** section lists its bindings and shows Permissions, Settings, and Drag in that library.

A module option named `can` is a function. The module calls it before and during an interaction. The module cancels the interaction when the function returns false. A module that changes the document wraps the change and the next render in one [undo transaction](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/runtime.md#undo-transactions). Modules show and speak their own text in the widget's language. Each language loads on first use. Pass `messages` to a module to replace a text.

### Permissions

Permissions answers `can(name)` for each entry of [`static permissions`](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/options-actions.md#element-permissions), true in edit mode and, in read mode, while the author has granted the permission. `PermissionsCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/permissions`; the bindings are `usePermissions`, `usePermissions`, `permissionsStore`, and `injectPermissions` for React, Vue, Svelte, and Angular.

`data-ww-can="name"` hides a shadow element while `can(name)` is false, `data-ww-can="edit"` shows it in edit mode only, and `data-ww-can-mode="disable"` makes it inert instead. The example is in the **Modules** section of the library. See [Permissions](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#permissions).

A component that sits in the shadow tree of another widget has no editing state of its own. It asks the surrounding widget, and answers when the widget's permissions change. The React, Angular, and Svelte bindings have `useWidgetPermissions(host)`, `injectWidgetPermissions()`, and `widgetPermissions(host)` for it. A Vue component renders in the widget's own shadow root, so `usePermissions()` already answers for the widget.

### Settings

Settings turns declarations into reflected attributes, entries of the Widget drawer, and controls bound with `data-ww-setting="name"`. `SettingsCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/settings`; the bindings are `useSettings`, `useSettings`, `settingsStore` with `withSettings`, and `injectSettings`.

Each setting becomes a reflected attribute and an entry of the Widget drawer. A boolean that defaults to true uses a negative attribute such as `no-show-chart`. The example is in the **Modules** section of the library. See [Settings](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#settings).

The `label`, `description`, and `placeholder` of a setting may be functions of the widget, and so may those of a choice of a `select`. The core asks the function whenever it shows the text, and `editorOptions()` gives the editor the answer. `labelOf(name, choice?)` returns the label in the widget's language. Use a function for a text that the widget keeps in its own catalog, and type its parameter by what it reads.

The same holds for the texts of `static options`, `static actions`, `static optionGroups`, and `static permissions`: `label`, `description`, `placeholder`, `confirm`, `disabledReason`, and the `label` and `description` of a choice. The editor reads plain maps, so the widget answers them. The classes from `createReactWidget()`, `createVueWidget()`, and `createAngularWidget()` do it on the instance. In Svelte, `withDeclarations(Base)` in `customElement.extend` does it, and `withSettings` and `withExercise` do it for `options` and `actions`. A plain element calls `resolveDeclarations(widget, map)` from `@webwriter/widget` in its own getter, and merges `editorOptions()` for its settings.

```js
import {resolveDeclarations} from "@webwriter/widget"
import {SettingsCore} from "@webwriter/widget/settings"

// Texts that are functions of the widget: asked whenever the editor reads them.
const german = widget => widget.lang === "de"

class WwSpeedDial extends HTMLElement {
  static settings = {
    speed: {
      type: Number,
      default: 1,
      min: 0.5,
      max: 4,
      step: 0.5,
      label: widget => ({_: german(widget) ? "Tempo" : "Speed"}),
      description: widget => ({_: german(widget) ? "Wie schnell der Lauf fortschreitet." : "How fast the run advances."}),
    },
    unit: {
      type: "select",
      default: "kmh",
      label: widget => ({_: german(widget) ? "Einheit" : "Unit"}),
      options: [
        {value: "kmh", label: widget => ({_: german(widget) ? "Kilometer pro Stunde" : "Kilometers per hour"})},
        {value: "mph", label: widget => ({_: german(widget) ? "Meilen pro Stunde" : "Miles per hour"})},
      ],
    },
  }

  // Other drawer entries. Their texts may be functions too.
  static options = {
    caption: {type: String, label: widget => ({_: german(widget) ? "Beschriftung" : "Caption"})},
  }

  #settings = new SettingsCore(this)
  #unsubscribe

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `
      <label><span data-ww-setting-label="speed"></span> <input type="number" data-ww-setting="speed"></label>
      <select data-ww-setting="unit"></select>
      <output></output>
    `
    this.#settings.defineProperties()
  }

  // The editor reads plain maps: answer the functions of `static options` and add one entry per setting.
  get options() {
    return {...resolveDeclarations(this, WwSpeedDial.options), ...this.#settings.editorOptions()}
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#settings.connect()
    this.#unsubscribe = this.#settings.subscribe(() => this.#render())
    this.#render()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#unsubscribe?.()
    this.#settings.disconnect()
  }

  #render() {
    const unit = String(this.#settings.get("unit"))
    this.shadowRoot.querySelector("output").textContent = `${this.#settings.get("speed")} ${this.#settings.labelOf("unit", unit)}`
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-speed-dial", WwSpeedDial)
```

### Shortcuts

Shortcuts runs an action of `static actions` from a key. `ShortcutsCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/shortcuts`; the bindings are `useShortcuts`, `useShortcuts`, `shortcutsStore`, and `injectShortcuts`.

Declare `shortcut` and `can` on an action. Mark a button with `data-ww-shortcut="action"`. A key runs the method of the same name on the widget. The core has `keysOf(action)`, `labelsOf(action)`, and `running`. The options are `rendered`, `apple`, and `messages`. See [Shortcuts](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#shortcuts).

A method that returns `false` had nothing to do, such as Escape with nothing to cancel. It declines the key: the key goes to the next action that declares it, and to the page when none takes it. Any other result, also `undefined` and a promise, takes the key. In the bindings the method is the handler that the widget supplies for the action: a handler of `useShortcuts()` or `useActions()` in React, a function that `defineExpose()` gives in Vue, a function of `injectActions()` in Angular, and a method of the class in `customElement.extend` in Svelte.

Keys typed in a text field, a text role, or an editable region belong to it. A key that must run there, such as Ctrl+Enter to run code, is declared as an object in `shortcut`: `{key: "Mod+Enter", inText: true}`, alone or in the list. Use it for a key that types nothing, a combination with Ctrl, ⌘, or Alt, Escape, or a function key. See [Keys in text fields](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#keys-in-text-fields). `data-ww-shortcuts="off"` on an element leaves every key inside it alone, for a part with its own keymap. `data-ww-shortcuts="on"` on a component with a closed shadow root says that it holds no text entry. A key is handled only when it comes from inside the widget, so give the widget something focusable, such as a stage with `tabindex="0"`. When an action declares a key, the core warns once in development if the template holds nothing that can take the focus. The check runs after the first `refresh()` that follows a render that put something other than styles into the shadow root, so a widget that renders its stage later is not reported for the renders before it. A core that is never refreshed is checked one frame after `connect()`.

```js
import {ShortcutsCore} from "@webwriter/widget/shortcuts"

class WwCounter extends HTMLElement {
  static actions = {
    increase: {label: {_: "Increase"}, shortcut: "ArrowUp"},
    reset: {label: {_: "Reset"}, shortcut: "Escape"},
  }

  #shortcuts = new ShortcutsCore(this)
  #count = 0

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `
      <div tabindex="0"><output>0</output></div>
      <button data-ww-shortcut="increase">+</button>
    `
    this.shadowRoot.querySelector("button").addEventListener("click", () => this.increase())
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#shortcuts.connect()
    this.#shortcuts.refresh()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#shortcuts.disconnect()
  }

  increase() {
    this.#show(this.#count + 1)
  }

  reset() {
    // Nothing to reset: decline the key, so that the page can use Escape.
    if (this.#count === 0) return false
    this.#show(0)
  }

  #show(count) {
    this.#count = count
    this.shadowRoot.querySelector("output").textContent = String(count)
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-counter", WwCounter)
```

### Drag

Drag picks up items and drops them on targets by pointer, keyboard, or click. `DragCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/drag`; the bindings are `useDrag`, `useDrag`, `dragStore`, and `injectDrag`.

Mark items with `data-ww-drag="kind"` and targets with `data-ww-drop="kind"`. The core has `item`, the element being dragged or picked up, and `via`, which is `"pointer"`, `"keyboard"`, `"click"`, or null. The options are `can`, `rendered`, `messages`, `lift`, `duration`, `easing`, and `viewport`. The module also exports the types `DragCommitDetail`, `DragPickDetail`, `DragEffect`, and `DragViewport`.

| Marker | Goes on | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `data-ww-drag="kind"` | An item, or a `<slot>` | An item of this kind. On a `<slot>` the assigned authored elements are the items. |
| `data-ww-key` | An item | Its identity. The events report it as `key`. |
| `data-ww-drag-handle` | A part of an item | Only this part starts the drag, and only this part gets `touch-action: none`, so the rest of the item scrolls by touch. |
| `data-ww-drag-via="pointer keyboard click"` | An item or its `<slot>` | The ways the item is picked up. Without it all three work. An item that leaves out `keyboard` needs another way to be moved without a pointer. |
| `data-ww-drag-effect="move\|copy\|link"` | An item or its `<slot>` | `copy` leaves the item where it is. `link` draws a connector from the item to the pointer. The default is `move`. |
| `data-ww-drag-axis="x\|y"` | An item | The item moves along this axis only. |
| `data-ww-drop="kind …"` | A target | The kinds the target accepts. |
| `data-ww-drop-position="index"` | A target | The target also resolves a place among its items. |
| `data-ww-drop-position="point"` | A target | The target resolves a point on its surface. `data-ww-drop-grid="step"` snaps it. |
| `data-ww-drop-space="world"` | A point target that is the window of a canvas viewport | The point is in the viewport's world coordinates. Pass the viewport as the `viewport` option. See [Dropping into a viewport](#dropping-into-a-viewport). |
| `data-ww-drop-max="n"` | A target | The capacity. `data-ww-drop-full="swap"` accepts an item when the target is full and reports the occupant as `displaced`. |
| `data-ww-drop-linked="key …"` | A target of links | The keys of the items linked to it, so that capacity and swap hold for links too. |
| `data-ww-label` | An item or a target | Its name in announcements. |

The events are `ww-dragpick`, on the item, and `ww-dragcommit`, on the target. Both are cancelable and bubble. `ww-dragpick` has `detail.candidates`, from which a handler can remove targets. `ww-dragcommit` has `detail` with `item`, `key`, `kind`, `effect`, `source`, `target`, `displaced`, `index`, `before`, `x`, `y`, and `slot`. `index` and `before` are set for an index target and null otherwise. `x` and `y` are set for a point target and null otherwise: the place of the item's top-left corner in the target's own coordinates, snapped to `data-ww-drop-grid`.

The example is in the **Modules** section of the library. For items that the widget renders, update the widget's state in the `ww-dragcommit` handler. For an authored child that moves, the core puts it before the item at `detail.before`. The commit event and the render after it form one undo step. See [Drag](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#drag).

### Viewport

Viewport zooms and pans one window onto larger content. `ViewportCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/viewport`; the bindings are `useViewport`, `useViewport`, `viewportStore`, and `injectViewport`.

Mark the window with `data-ww-viewport`, `data-ww-viewport="canvas"`, or `data-ww-viewport="external"`. Add `data-ww-viewport-controls` for the zoom buttons and `data-ww-viewport-save="name"` to keep the view in an attribute. See [Viewport](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#viewport).

The core has `getSnapshot()` with `x`, `y`, `scale`, `min`, `max`, `width`, and `height`. A world point `w` is drawn at `w * scale + (x, y)` in CSS pixels from the top-left corner of the window. The methods are `zoomBy(factor, about?)`, `zoomTo(scale, about?)`, `panBy(dx, dy)`, `fit(call?)`, `fitted()`, `centerOn(point, scale?, motion?)`, `setView(view, motion?)`, `autoPan(clientX, clientY)`, `autoPanWhile(source)`, `toWorld(clientX, clientY)`, `toClient(worldX, worldY)`, and `contentChanged()`. The module also exports the types `ViewportFitCall`, `ViewportFitDetail`, `ViewportFitOptions`, `ViewportFollow`, `ViewportInsets`, `ViewportMotion`, `ViewportPointerSource`, `ViewportSnapshot`, `ViewportStart`, `ViewportWheel`, and `WorldBox`.

| Declaration | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `data-ww-viewport` | The window. By default it is a scroll container: panning is its scroll position, and zoom is the CSS `zoom` of its first child. |
| `data-ww-viewport="canvas"` | The window is a surface that the widget draws. The core keeps `x`, `y`, and `scale`, and the widget applies them. |
| `data-ww-viewport="external"` | A library owns the view. Pass `adapter` so that the buttons and keys can drive it. |
| `data-ww-viewport-zoom="min max"` | The zoom limits. The default is `0.25 4`. |
| `data-ww-viewport-fit="content\|width\|none"` | What fit shows. The default is `content`. |
| `data-ww-viewport-pan="x\|y"` | Restricts input panning to one axis. |
| `data-ww-viewport-save="name"` | The widget attribute that keeps the view as `x y scale`, the world point in the center of the window and the scale. |
| `data-ww-viewport-controls` | An element that receives four buttons: zoom out, zoom in, the current percent, and fit. |

The options are `can`, `canSave`, `bounds`, `margin`, `adapter`, `rendered`, `messages`, and the options behind the attributes of the subsections below: `wheel`, `start`, `resize`, and `fit`. An attribute on the window wins over its option. `bounds` returns the extent of the content in world coordinates for the canvas form. Fit shows it, and panning stays within it. `margin` is how far in CSS pixels the content can be panned past each edge of `bounds`. Call `contentChanged()` when the answer of `bounds` changes without a render.

#### Wheel

`data-ww-viewport-wheel` (option `wheel`) says what the plain wheel does over the window. `Ctrl` or `⌘` with the wheel and a pinch on a trackpad zoom in every mode.

| Value | The plain wheel |
|---|---|
| `pan` | Pans. This is the default. |
| `zoom` | Zooms about the pointer. A sideways wheel (one with only `deltaX`) still pans. |
| `page` | Is left to the page, so that the page scrolls over the window. This applies to the canvas form. A scroll container scrolls natively anyway. |

Use `zoom` for a surface that fills the screen, such as a diagram editor, and `page` for a window that sits inside a longer page.

#### Start view and centering

The first view of a window is applied once, when the window first has a size. The order is a view carried over from a replaced window, the saved view, the start view, and then the fit. A saved view always wins over the start view.

`data-ww-viewport-start` takes `fit` or `x y scale`. The numbers are the world point in the center of the window and the scale, as in `data-ww-viewport-save`. The scale is optional and defaults to 1. The option `start` takes a value or a function that the core asks once.

| `start` value | First view |
|---|---|
| `"fit"` | The fitted view, as if there were no start view. |
| `{centre, scale?}` | A world point in the center of the window. |
| `{x, y, scale?}` | The position of the world's origin, in CSS pixels from the corner of the window. |
| `{box}` | A box of the world, fitted once. The view stays there until something changes it. |

`centerOn(point, scale?, motion?)` puts a world point in the center of the window and optionally sets the scale. `setView({x, y, scale?})` sets where the world's origin is drawn, and `setView({scale})` sets the scale about the center. Both return a promise that resolves when the view is there. `{animate: true}` glides for 350 ms, and a number is the duration in milliseconds. The animation never runs for a reader who prefers reduced motion, and any other change of the view ends it, which also settles the promise. A call before the window has a size is applied when the window opens. After either call the view is no longer a fitted view.

#### Fitting

A fit shows the content in the window. The content is the box that `fit.target` returns, or else the box that `bounds` returns, in the canvas form, and the first child of the window in the scroll form. A view counts as fitted from its first view, when there is no saved or start view, and after `fit()`, the fit button, and the `0` key. It stays fitted until something else changes it: a zoom, a pan, `zoomTo`, `zoomBy`, `panBy`, `setView`, `centerOn`, or a start or saved view.

| Attribute | Option `fit` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `data-ww-viewport-fit-padding="px"` | `padding` | Room kept free around the content (canvas form). |
| `data-ww-viewport-fit-max="scale"` | `maxScale` | The largest scale a fit chooses, so that small content is not enlarged. |
| `data-ww-viewport-fit-inset="top right bottom left"` | `inset` | A part of the window that something else covers, such as a drawer. One to four numbers, as CSS margins. The option takes a number or `{top, right, bottom, left}` (canvas form). |
| `data-ww-viewport-follow="all\|window\|none"` | `follow` | When a fitted view fits again by itself. |
| | `target` | A function that returns the box to fit instead of `bounds`, such as the gates instead of the whole board. The fit button and the `0` key use it too (canvas form). |

`fit` may also be a function, which the core asks at every fit. `follow` takes these values.

- `all` (the default) fits again when the window or the content changes size.
- `window` fits again only when the window changes size.
- `none` never fits again: the view is fitted once and then left alone.

A view that is not fitted keeps its place when the window resizes. `data-ww-viewport-resize="offset|centre"` (option `resize`) says what stays still: the screen offset of the world (the default), or the world point in the center of the window.

`fit(call?)` returns a promise with the snapshot of the view. The call takes `animate`, which works as for `centerOn()` and applies to the canvas form only, a `follow` for this fit alone, and `box`, a box of the world to fit instead of the content (canvas form). `fit({follow: "none"})` fits once and leaves the view alone, and `fit({box})` does the same for a chosen box. In the external form the library fits and ignores the options.

`fitted()` returns a promise that resolves when the view is a fitted one that is up to date: at once if it is, and otherwise after the next fit. It rejects with an `AbortError` when the core disconnects first. Await it before code that needs the view, such as a first measurement.

After every fit the host dispatches `ww-viewportfit`. Its `detail` is the snapshot and a `reason`: `open` for the first view, `request` for `fit()`, the fit button, or the `0` key, and `follow` for a fit that the core made because the window or the content changed size.

#### Panning at the edge

`autoPan(clientX, clientY)` is one step of panning for a pointer in a band at the edge of the window. The band is 64 pixels wide, or a quarter of the window when that is smaller. The view moves towards what lies beyond, up to 16 pixels per call and faster the closer the pointer is to the edge. The method returns whether the view moved, does nothing for a pointer outside the window, and stops at the limits of the view.

Call it once per animation frame during a drag that began elsewhere. `autoPanWhile(source)` does that until the gesture ends. `source` is any object with `last.clientX`, `last.clientY`, and an `ended` abort signal, such as a `PointerGesture` from `@webwriter/widget/gesture`. [Drag](#drag) calls `autoPan` by itself for a target in world coordinates.

#### Dropping into a viewport

A drag that ends on the window of a canvas viewport gives the point in the world, under the pan and zoom of the view. Mark the window as a point target in world coordinates with `data-ww-drop-space="world"` and pass the `ViewportCore` as the `viewport` option of the `DragCore`.

`ww-dragcommit` then reports `x` and `y` as the world point under the top-left corner of the lifted item. `data-ww-drop-grid` is in world units. The arrow keys move a keyboard drop by one grid cell, or by 10 world units without a grid and 1 with Shift. The view pans while the pointer is held at the edge of the window. Without the `viewport` option the target is measured as an ordinary point target, and the core warns in development.

The example takes a chip from a sidebar and places it on the board. The wheel zooms, the first view is centered on a point, and the fit leaves some room around the content.

```js
import {DragCore} from "@webwriter/widget/drag"
import {ViewportCore} from "@webwriter/widget/viewport"

class WwChipBoard extends HTMLElement {
  #viewport = new ViewportCore(this, {
    bounds: () => ({x: 0, y: 0, width: 1200, height: 800}),
    wheel: "zoom",
    start: {centre: {x: 200, y: 150}, scale: 1},
    fit: {padding: 24, maxScale: 1},
  })
  // The target is a point target in world coordinates: Drag asks this viewport where a drop lands.
  #drag = new DragCore(this, {viewport: this.#viewport})
  #world
  #unsubscribe
  #chips = 0

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `
      <style>
        .board { position: relative; height: 260px; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid #c8c8c8; background: #f4f4f5; }
        .world { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 0; height: 0; transform-origin: 0 0; }
        .chip { position: absolute; width: 60px; height: 30px; box-sizing: border-box; border: 1px solid #555; background: #bfdbfe; }
        [data-ww-viewport-controls] { position: absolute; right: 6px; top: 6px; }
      </style>
      <div data-ww-drag="chip" data-ww-drag-effect="copy" data-ww-key="and" data-ww-label="AND gate" tabindex="0">AND</div>
      <div class="board" data-ww-viewport="canvas" data-ww-drop="chip" data-ww-drop-position="point"
           data-ww-drop-space="world" data-ww-drop-grid="20" aria-label="Board">
        <div class="world"></div>
        <span data-ww-viewport-controls></span>
      </div>
      <button>Whole board</button>
      <output></output>
    `
    const root = this.shadowRoot
    this.#world = root.querySelector("div.world")
    root.querySelector(".board").addEventListener("ww-dragcommit", event => this.#place(event))
    root.querySelector("button").addEventListener("click", () => this.#viewport.fit({animate: true}))
    this.addEventListener("ww-viewportfit", event => this.#fitted(event))
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#viewport.connect()
    this.#drag.connect()
    this.#unsubscribe = this.#viewport.subscribe(() => this.#show())
    this.#viewport.refresh()
    this.#show()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#unsubscribe?.()
    this.#drag.disconnect()
    this.#viewport.disconnect()
  }

  #place(event) {
    const {x, y} = event.detail
    if (x === null || y === null) return
    const chip = document.createElement("div")
    chip.className = "chip"
    chip.id = `chip-${this.#chips++}`
    chip.style.left = `${x}px`
    chip.style.top = `${y}px`
    this.#world.append(chip)
  }

  #fitted(event) {
    this.shadowRoot.querySelector("output").textContent = event.detail.reason
  }

  #show() {
    const {x, y, scale} = this.#viewport.getSnapshot()
    this.#world.style.transform = `translate(${x}px, ${y}px) scale(${scale})`
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-chip-board", WwChipBoard)
```

```js
import {ViewportCore} from "@webwriter/widget/viewport"

class WwFloorPlan extends HTMLElement {
  static observedAttributes = ["src"]

  #viewport = new ViewportCore(this)

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `
      <div style="height: 300px" data-ww-viewport data-ww-viewport-zoom="0.5 4" data-ww-viewport-save="view" aria-label="Floor plan">
        <img width="1200" height="800" alt="">
      </div>
      <div data-ww-viewport-controls></div>
    `
  }

  attributeChangedCallback(name, before, value) {
    this.shadowRoot.querySelector("img").src = value ?? ""
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#viewport.connect()
    this.#viewport.refresh()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#viewport.disconnect()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-floor-plan", WwFloorPlan)
```

### Help

Help shows an overlay with one label for each marked control. `HelpCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/help`; the bindings are `useHelp`, `useHelp`, `helpStore`, and `injectHelp`.

Mark a control with `data-ww-help="text"` and the button that opens the overlay with `data-ww-help-toggle`. See [Help](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#help).

```js
import {HelpCore} from "@webwriter/widget/help"

class WwToolbar extends HTMLElement {
  #help = new HelpCore(this)

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `
      <button data-ww-help="Add a node" data-ww-help-order="1">Add</button>
      <button data-ww-help="Remove the selected node" data-ww-help-order="2">Remove</button>
      <div tabindex="0" data-ww-help="The diagram"><slot></slot></div>
      <button data-ww-help-toggle aria-label="Help">?</button>
    `
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#help.connect()
    this.#help.refresh()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#help.disconnect()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-toolbar", WwToolbar)
```

### Scene

Scene draws nodes, shapes, paths, text, and images, and reports what the reader does with them. `SceneCore` and `sceneElements` are in `@webwriter/widget/scene`; the bindings are `useScene`, `useScene`, `sceneStore`, and `injectScene`.

Write `<ww-scene>` with `<ww-node>`, `<ww-shape>`, `<ww-path>`, `<ww-text>`, `<ww-image>`, `<ww-group>`, and `<ww-sprites>` in the shadow root. Register the elements from `sceneElements`. For WebGL rendering, register `PixiScene` from `@webwriter/widget/scene/pixi` as `ww-scene`. Only this import bundles `pixi.js`. Use `webglAvailable()` from `@webwriter/widget/scene` to select the renderer. See [Scene](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#scene).

The core has `marquee` in its snapshot and the methods `extent()`, `measureText(text, source?)`, `toScene(clientX, clientY)`, `toClient(x, y)`, `itemAt(point, {client}?)`, `itemsAt(point, {client}?)`, `endsOf(path)`, `wiresAt(reference)`, `toSVG(options?)`, `toImage(options?)`, `printing`, `restyle()`, and `remeasure()`, and the getter `ready`. The methods that name a scene answer for the widget's first `ww-scene`. The options are `can`, `viewport`, `rendered`, `messages`, and `undoHost`. `@webwriter/widget/scene` also exports the event types `SelectDetail`, `MoveDetail`, `MovingDetail`, `ResizeDetail`, `ResizingDetail`, `ConnectDetail`, `ConnectingDetail`, `ReconnectDetail`, `DisconnectDetail`, `ActivateDetail`, `ContextDetail`, `BackgroundDetail`, `HitDetail`, and `SceneErrorDetail`, and the types `PointerPoint`, `PortEnd`, `SnapshotOptions`, `ImageOptions`, `TextFont`, `TextSize`, `UndoHost`, `SceneItem`, `ScenePath`, `Point`, and `Rect`.

`toSVG(options?)` returns the first scene as a standalone SVG document, or `null` for an empty scene. `toImage(options?)` returns a `Promise<Blob>`, PNG by default. Both work with every renderer, and `printing` is true while the document is printed. A scene prints correctly without code of the widget, also `PixiScene`. See [Picture and print](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#picture-and-print).

`can` is a function `(action, item, port?)` or a map from an action to a permission name, such as `{move: "allowMoving"}`. The actions are `select`, `move`, `resize`, and `connect`. For a connection that starts or ends at a port, a function also gets the port element, so that it can refuse one port and not the whole node. `viewport` takes the `ViewportCore` of a [Viewport](#viewport) for a scene that is the window of a canvas viewport. `undoHost` is the element on which a commit opens its undo step. The editor takes a step only from an event that starts on the widget itself, so a core in a component inside the widget passes `"outermost"` (the host at the top of the shadow roots above the scene), the widget, or a function that returns it. Without it the step starts on the host of the scene's shadow root.

| Element | Attributes | Draws |
|---|---|---|
| `ww-scene` | `select="none\|single\|multiple"`, `grid`, `move-step`, `connect-click`, `background="dots\|lines"`, `background-spacing` | The scene. `grid` snaps moves and resizes to its multiples. `move-step` is how far an arrow key moves an item (five times as far with Shift). Without it the step is the grid, or 1 and 10 without a grid. `connect-click` lets a click on a port pick a wire up. `background` draws a grid below everything that follows the view. |
| `ww-node` | `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `resizable`, `keep-ratio`, `outline="rect\|rounded\|circle\|ellipse"`, `radius` | The HTML content of the node at a scene position. `outline` is the shape where a path ends at the whole node. The selection outline follows it. |
| `ww-group` | `x`, `y`, `scale`, `frame`, `padding`, `label`, `radius` | Its children, moved and scaled together. With `frame` it is also drawn as a box around its members. |
| `ww-shape` | `kind="rect\|circle\|polygon"`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `r`, `points`, `radius`, `rotate`, `resizable` | A shape. A circle is placed by its center. `radius` rounds the corners of a rect. `rotate` turns a rect about its center and a polygon about `x`, `y`. A rect that is `resizable` has handles while it is selected. |
| `ww-path` | `from`, `to`, `route="straight\|step\|curve\|arc\|orthogonal"`, `bend`, `loop`, `waypoints`, `marker-start`, `marker-end`, `hit-width`, `rewire` | A line between two ends, each written `node:port` or `node`. A path without `from` and `to` follows its `points` property, relative to its `x` and `y`. |
| `ww-text` | `x`, `y`, `rotate`; as a label also `at`, `along`, `side`, `gap`, `follow` | Its text content. Inside a `ww-path` it is a label of the path. |
| `ww-image` | `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `href`, `resizable` | A picture. The `source` property takes an image source such as a canvas. |
| `ww-sprites` | `texture` | A batch of sprites from its `items` property. Pixi renderer only. |

Every element also takes `data-ww-key`, `selected`, `selectable`, `movable`, and `aria-label`, and the [constraints](#constraints) below. A path refers to a node by its key, and the events report keys. Style drawn elements with CSS: they take `stroke`, `fill`, and the font properties from their computed style. `--ww-scene-selection` sets the color of the selection outline and of the handles. A port is an element with `data-ww-port="name"` inside a node. `data-ww-link="kind"` on a port starts a wire. `data-ww-accept="kind …"` on a port accepts wires of these kinds. `data-ww-side="left|right|top|bottom"` sets the side where a path leaves a port. Without it the port faces the nearest edge of its node.

| Event | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ww-select` | The reader asks for a selection. `detail.keys` and `detail.items`. |
| `ww-move` | The reader moved items. `detail.items` has the key and the new `x` and `y` of each item. `detail.dx` and `detail.dy` give the movement of the lead item. `detail.pointer` is where the pointer was, or null for a move by keyboard. |
| `ww-moving` | A step of a move, and once more when it is over. It informs, writes nothing, and cannot be canceled. `detail` is that of `ww-move` with `state` (`move` or `end`) and `committed`. |
| `ww-resize` | The reader resized a node, or a rect or an image that is `resizable`. `detail` has `key`, `item`, `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`. |
| `ww-resizing` | A step of a resize, and once more when it is over. It is to a resize what `ww-moving` is to a move, with `state` `resize` or `end`. |
| `ww-connect` | The reader connected two ports, or two whole nodes. `detail` has `from`, `to` (`node:port`, or `node`), `kind`, `source`, `target`, and `pointer`. |
| `ww-reconnect` | The reader took an end of a wire to another port. `detail` has `path`, `end`, the new `from` and `to`, `previous`, `kind`, `source`, `target`, and `pointer`. |
| `ww-disconnect` | The reader let an end of a wire go where no port is. `detail` has `path`, `end`, `from`, `to`, `kind`, and `pointer`. |
| `ww-connecting` | A wire is held. `detail` says which port it is over. |
| `ww-activate` | A click, a double click, or Enter or Space on an item, also on one that is selected already. |
| `ww-context` | A context menu, the menu key, or a long press by touch, on an item or on the background. |
| `ww-background` | A click, a double click, or a long press on the background. |
| `ww-ready` | The first layout has settled. |
| `ww-sceneerror` | The scene cannot draw something. `detail.code` is `load`, `unsupported`, or `webgl`. |

All events bubble out of the widget's shadow root. `pointer` is `{x, y, clientX, clientY}`: the scene point and the client point.

```js
import {SceneCore, sceneElements} from "@webwriter/widget/scene"

for (const [tag, constructor] of Object.entries(sceneElements)) {
  if (!customElements.get(tag)) customElements.define(tag, constructor)
}

class WwBoxes extends HTMLElement {
  static observedAttributes = ["boxes"]

  static permissions = {
    allowMoving: {label: {_: "Learners may move the boxes"}, attribute: "allow-moving"},
  }

  #scene = new SceneCore(this, {can: {move: "allowMoving"}})

  constructor() {
    super()
    const root = this.attachShadow({mode: "open"})
    root.innerHTML = `
      <style>ww-scene { height: 240px; border: 1px solid #c8c8c8 }</style>
      <ww-scene select="single" grid="10"></ww-scene>
    `
    root.querySelector("ww-scene").addEventListener("ww-move", event => this.#move(event))
  }

  get boxes() {
    return JSON.parse(this.getAttribute("boxes") ?? "[]")
  }

  attributeChangedCallback() {
    this.#render()
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#scene.connect()
    this.#render()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#scene.disconnect()
  }

  // The scene runs the event in one undo step: the attribute is written inside it.
  #move(event) {
    const moved = new Map(event.detail.items.map(item => [item.key, item]))
    const boxes = this.boxes.map(box => (moved.has(box.id) ? {...box, x: moved.get(box.id).x, y: moved.get(box.id).y} : box))
    this.setAttribute("boxes", JSON.stringify(boxes))
  }

  #render() {
    const scene = this.shadowRoot.querySelector("ww-scene")
    for (const box of this.boxes) {
      const node = scene.querySelector(`[data-ww-key="${box.id}"]`) ?? this.#create(scene, box.id)
      node.setAttribute("x", String(box.x))
      node.setAttribute("y", String(box.y))
    }
    this.#scene.refresh()
  }

  #create(scene, id) {
    const node = document.createElement("ww-node")
    node.dataset.wwKey = id
    node.toggleAttribute("movable", true)
    node.textContent = `Box ${id}`
    scene.append(node)
    return node
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-boxes", WwBoxes)
```

- The scene changes no document. Each interaction previews and then ends in one cancelable event that bubbles. The widget applies the change to its model. The event and the render after it form one undo step. `preventDefault()` refuses the change.
- The selection is the widget's. The scene reads the `selected` attribute and asks for a change with `ww-select`.
- The core asks `can` before a selection, move, resize, or connection, during it, and before it commits. An interaction ends when the answer turns false.
- Pointer, touch, and keyboard all work. A node that is `selectable` or `movable` takes focus. Arrow keys move the selection and commit after a short rest. Moves and wires are announced in a live region.
- The scene writes no position or size to its elements. A preview is a Web Animation that ends with the interaction. A `selectable` or `movable` node without a `tabindex` gets `tabindex="0"`.
- Drawn elements and `ww-scene` have custom states for CSS: `:state(hover)` on a drawn item, `:state(failed)` on an image that did not load, `:state(rewiring)` on a path whose end is held, and `:state(wiring)` and `:state(marquee)` on the scene. `ww-scene::part(link)` is the pending wire, `ww-scene::part(resize)` the handles of a rect or image, and `ww-node::part(handle)` the handles of a node.
- A scene inside a scrolling `data-ww-viewport` is zoomed from outside. Pass `viewport` only for the canvas form.
- Call `restyle()` after a style change that no observer sees, and `remeasure()` when ports moved without a change of the document. A change of document theme is not one of them: the scene restyles itself after `ww-themechange`, a change of `prefers-color-scheme`, and a change of class, style, or `data-theme` on the widget or the page.
- Mark a control inside a node with `data-ww-control` and the scene keeps its size on the screen while the view is zoomed out. The scene writes `--ww-scene-zoom` and `--ww-scene-counter` on its layer for this. See [Theme and zoom](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#theme-and-zoom).
- A scene element has a property for each of its attributes `route`, `bend`, `loop`, `waypoints`, `rewire`, `outline`, `scale`, `side`, and `at`. Setting the property writes the attribute, and `null` removes it, so a framework that assigns a prop as a property, as React and Vue do, passes them like any other prop.

#### Paths, markers, and labels

A path ends at a port (`from="a:out"`) or at a whole node (`from="a"`). A node that declares an `outline` is met on that outline, and a node without an `outline` is met at its center. An attached path follows its nodes while they are dragged, moved by keyboard, or resized, and follows the nodes of a group that moves. A path without `from` and `to` is drawn along its `points` property instead.

| Attribute of a `ww-path` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `route` | `straight` (the default), `step`, `curve`, `arc`, or `orthogonal`. `step` and `curve` leave a whole node on the side that faces the other end. |
| `bend` | A number. The path becomes an arc. The control point of the arc is `bend` times the length of the line between the ends away from its middle, to the left of the way from start to end when `bend` is positive. Two paths between the same nodes, one each way, with the same `bend` stay apart. `route="arc"` without `bend` has 0.25, and `bend="0"` is a line. |
| `loop` | An angle in degrees, 0 up and clockwise. A path from a node to itself becomes a loop that leaves and returns where the outline of the node lets it out. An empty value is 45. |
| `waypoints` | The widget's own route: `x,y` pairs, each from the start end, or from the end with `e:` in front, as in `waypoints="20,0 20,-60 e:-20,-60 e:-20,0"`. The route follows its nodes because the points are relative to the ends. |
| `marker-start`, `marker-end` | `none`, `arrow`, `open-arrow`, `triangle`, `triangle-filled`, `diamond`, `diamond-filled`, `circle`, or `circle-open`. |
| `hit-width` | The width, in pixels, of the band in which the path takes the pointer. The default is 12. |
| `rewire` | Lets the reader take an end to another port. See [Wires](#wires). |

`route="orthogonal"` draws horizontal and vertical segments. Each end leaves at its side. The middle segment runs halfway between the ends if no other node is in the way. Otherwise it runs at the nearest free place beside the nodes in the way, 12 pixels clear, and if there is none, the path goes out, across above or below, and in. The route does not avoid other paths and is laid out again whenever a node moves, so use it for scenes of tens of nodes. For more nodes, compute the route in the widget and pass `waypoints`.

A marker has the stroke color of the path and is 8 pixels plus twice the stroke width long. `--ww-scene-marker-size` sets another length. A hollow marker (`triangle`, `diamond`, and `circle-open`) is filled with `--ww-scene-marker-fill`, which is none by default. The path ends at the base of the marker, and an open arrow ends at its tip. A marker shrinks on a path that is too short for it and is never dashed. Markers and labels take the pointer with their path and are part of its selection outline.

A `ww-text` inside a `ww-path` is a label of the path. A path may have several. A label is drawn with the path, takes the pointer with it, and has no tab stop of its own. Label text is not part of the accessible name of the path, so set `aria-label` on a path whose label matters.

| Attribute of a label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `at` | `start`, `middle` (the default), `end`, or a fraction between 0 and 1 of the length of the path. |
| `along` | Pixels to move along the line, positive towards the end. |
| `side` | `on` the line (the default), or beside it: `left` or `right` of the way, `above`, or `below`. |
| `gap` | Pixels between the line and the box of the label when it is beside the line. The default is 4. |
| `follow` | Turns the label to the direction of the line, upright. `rotate` sets an angle instead. |

The example draws a small state machine. The states are circles, the two transitions between them are arcs with the same `bend`, and a loop leaves the busy state. Each transition has an arrow and a label. The scene shows a dotted background and a framed group, and sizes each state to its name with `measureText()`.

```js
import {SceneCore, sceneElements} from "@webwriter/widget/scene"

for (const [tag, element] of Object.entries(sceneElements)) {
  if (!customElements.get(tag)) customElements.define(tag, element)
}

const STATES = [{id: "idle", x: 40, y: 80}, {id: "busy", x: 260, y: 80}]
const TRANSITIONS = [
  {id: "go", from: "idle", to: "busy", label: "start", bend: 0.25},
  {id: "back", from: "busy", to: "idle", label: "stop", bend: 0.25},
  {id: "retry", from: "busy", to: "busy", label: "retry\nlater", loop: 45},
]

class WwStateMachine extends HTMLElement {
  #scene = new SceneCore(this)

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `
      <style>
        ww-scene { display: block; height: 260px; color: #334155; --ww-scene-grid-color: #94a3b8; }
        ww-node { display: grid; place-items: center; box-sizing: border-box; background: white; border: 2px solid #334155; }
        ww-path { stroke: #334155; stroke-width: 2px; }
        ww-path ww-text { fill: #1e293b; font-size: 13px; white-space: pre-line; background-color: white; padding: 0 4px; }
        ww-group { fill: #f1f5f9; stroke: #94a3b8; stroke-dasharray: 4 3; color: #64748b; }
      </style>
      <ww-scene select="single" background="dots" background-spacing="20"></ww-scene>
    `
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#scene.connect()
    this.#render()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#scene.disconnect()
  }

  #render() {
    const scene = this.shadowRoot.querySelector("ww-scene")
    const frame = document.createElement("ww-group")
    frame.toggleAttribute("frame", true)
    frame.setAttribute("label", "Machine")
    frame.setAttribute("padding", "16")
    scene.replaceChildren(frame)
    for (const state of STATES) {
      // Size a state to its name. The size is zero until the scene is connected.
      const width = Math.max(64, this.#scene.measureText(state.id, {fontSize: 14}).width + 24)
      const node = document.createElement("ww-node")
      node.dataset.wwKey = state.id
      node.setAttribute("x", String(state.x))
      node.setAttribute("y", String(state.y))
      node.setAttribute("width", String(width))
      node.setAttribute("height", "64")
      node.setAttribute("outline", "circle")
      node.textContent = state.id
      frame.append(node)
    }
    for (const transition of TRANSITIONS) {
      const path = document.createElement("ww-path")
      path.dataset.wwKey = transition.id
      path.setAttribute("from", transition.from)
      path.setAttribute("to", transition.to)
      if (transition.bend !== undefined) path.setAttribute("bend", String(transition.bend))
      if (transition.loop !== undefined) path.setAttribute("loop", String(transition.loop))
      path.setAttribute("marker-end", "arrow")
      path.setAttribute("hit-width", "24")
      const label = document.createElement("ww-text")
      label.setAttribute("side", "above")
      label.textContent = transition.label
      path.append(label)
      scene.append(path)
    }
    this.#scene.refresh()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-state-machine", WwStateMachine)
```

#### Shapes, text, groups, and the background

`ww-shape kind="rect"` takes `radius` for rounded corners. `rotate` (degrees, clockwise) turns a rect about its center, and a polygon and a text about their `x`, `y`.

A `ww-text` is a text of one or more lines at `x`, `y`. The scene reads these properties of its style.

- `white-space: pre-line` (also `pre` and `pre-wrap`) keeps the line breaks of its text. Otherwise line breaks are spaces. `line-height` sets the distance of the lines.
- `text-anchor` (`start`, `middle`, `end`) says which end of the lines is at `x`.
- `dominant-baseline` says what `y` is: the top of the text (the default), its middle (`middle` or `central`), its bottom (`text-after-edge`), or the alphabetic baseline of the first line (`alphabetic`). The Pixi renderer puts that baseline about 0.8 em below the top of the line.
- `stroke` and `stroke-width` make a halo under the letters. `background-color`, `padding`, and `border-radius` make a box behind it. A label of a path has them too.

`measureText(text, source?)` of the core (and of `ww-scene`) tells the size a text will have before anything is drawn: `{width, height, lines, lineHeight}` in scene pixels, with the widest line and the height of all lines. `source` is an element whose font is used, such as a `ww-text`, or some entries of a font (`{fontSize: 14}`; the other entries are `fontFamily`, `fontWeight`, `fontStyle`, and `lineHeight`). Without a `source` the font of the scene is used. `\n` breaks lines. Use it to size a node to its label. The result is zero until the scene has been connected. `extent()` includes texts with their padding, the markers and labels of paths, rotated outlines, and the frames of groups.

A `ww-group` with `frame` is drawn as a box around its members: nodes, drawn items, and other groups. `padding` is the distance in pixels (8 by default), `radius` rounds the corners, and `label` appears above the box. The box has the `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, and `stroke-dasharray` of the group and follows its members while they move. An empty group has no box. Where the group is selectable or movable, a press anywhere inside the box moves the group and what it holds.

`background="dots"` or `"lines"` on `ww-scene` draws a grid below everything, with its marks at the multiples of `background-spacing` (or of `grid`, or 20). The grid follows the view, covers the visible part of the scene, and is drawn as one tiled pattern. `--ww-scene-grid-color` and `--ww-scene-grid-size` (the radius of a dot, the width of a line) style it. It takes no pointer and is no part of `extent()`.

#### Reacting while the reader acts

The commit events (`ww-select`, `ww-move`, `ww-resize`, `ww-connect`, `ww-reconnect`, and `ww-disconnect`) are the place to change the model. The other events inform. They write nothing and cannot be canceled, except `ww-connecting` and `ww-context`, which say so. Each is sent on the item it is about. `ww-select`, `ww-background`, and `ww-ready` are sent on the scene.

- **`ww-moving`** comes for every step of a move by pointer or by keyboard, and once more after it. `detail.items` are where the items are shown now: previewed during the move, and where the attributes put them at its end (`state` is `end`, and `committed` says whether the widget took the move). Update what depends on a dragged item from it, such as a readout that follows the item, and keep the result out of the model. A move that is canceled ends with `end` and `committed: false`, and the display returns to the model. Paths that are attached to nodes follow the preview by themselves. `ww-resizing` is the same for a resize.
- **Where the pointer is.** `detail.pointer` of `ww-moving`, `ww-move`, `ww-connect`, and `ww-activate` is `{x, y, clientX, clientY}`, or null for the keyboard. Use the client point for a drop outside the scene, such as `document.elementFromPoint` for a trash can, and the scene point for a drop on something that is in the model.
- **`ww-activate`** comes after every click, also on an item that is selected already (then there is no `ww-select`), with `detail.count` 2 for a double click, and for Enter or Space (`via` is `keyboard`). `detail.item` is the item that a click acts on, as `ww-select` reports it: the nearest of the pressed item and the groups around it that is selectable or movable. `detail.hit` is the item that was pressed, such as a neuron inside a movable layer, `detail.groups` are the groups around it, and `detail.target` is the element that was pressed. `detail` also has `key`, `shiftKey`, `ctrlKey`, `altKey`, and `metaKey`. A click on a control inside a node (a button, a link, a field) is the control's and is not reported.
- **`ww-context`** comes for a context menu, the menu key, and a long press by touch. `detail.kind` is `node`, `path`, `shape`, `text`, `image`, `group`, `sprites`, or `background`. `detail.key`, `detail.hit`, `detail.item`, `detail.groups`, and `detail.target` say what was hit, `detail.point` says where (for the menu key, the middle of the item), and `detail.via` is `pointer`, `keyboard`, or `touch`. Cancel the event to keep the browser's menu away and show the widget's own. Where a long press by touch already means something (it adds to the selection in multiple selection and draws a marquee on the background), it is not a context menu.
- **`ww-background`** comes for a click, a double click, and a long press on the background, with `detail.gesture` of `click`, `dblclick`, or `longpress`, the scene `point`, `pointerType`, and the modifier keys. A drag is not a click. It also comes where nothing can be selected.
- **`ww-ready`** and `ready` say that the first layout has settled: the fonts are loaded, the nodes are measured, and the paths are drawn, so `extent()` is what it will stay. A scene that is not shown settles when it is. Fit a viewport to `extent()` then.

#### Wires

A port is an element with `data-ww-port`. It starts a wire with `data-ww-link="kind"` and takes wires with `data-ww-accept="kind …"`. By default a wire is dragged from a port to a port.

- **Capacity.** `data-ww-capacity="1"` on a port, or on a node, limits the wires at it. A port that is full starts no wire (also not by keyboard) and is not offered as a target, so the template does not have to take its attributes away. The count includes the paths with `from` or `to` at it. `can` is asked with the port as its third argument, to refuse a port by another rule.
- **Whole nodes.** `data-ww-link` and `data-ww-accept` on the `ww-node` itself make the whole node the place a wire starts and ends. A press anywhere on it draws a wire instead of moving it, so set the attributes only in the mode that draws wires. The wire is written with the bare key: `from="a" to="b"`. The target is the node under the pointer, within its outline. The keyboard starts a wire from a focused node with Enter.
- **Taking a wire from a port.** A `ww-path` with `rewire` (`to`, `from`, or `from to`; an empty value is `to`) lets the reader grab that end of the wire and take it to another port (`ww-reconnect`) or let it go where no port is (`ww-disconnect`). The end is grabbed at its port when that port starts no wire (it has no `data-ww-link`, or it is full), and on the path within 16 pixels of the end. A path with `rewire` takes the pointer in a band like a selectable one. While an end is held the path has `:state(rewiring)`. The kind of the wire is the kind of the end that stays. The widget changes `from` or `to` of the path, or removes it, and `preventDefault()` refuses. A click on the end that does not move it selects the path.
- **A click on a port.** `connect-click` on the scene lets a click on a port pick the wire up. The wire follows the pointer, a click on a port that takes it connects, and a click elsewhere or Escape cancels. Dragging still works.
- **While a wire is held**, `ww-connecting` is sent on the port it started at. `detail` has `from`, `to`, `kind`, `source`, `target`, `via` (`pointer`, `click`, or `keyboard`), `pointer`, and `state` (`move` for every step, once with `end` when the wire is put down). `from` and `to` are the ends the wire has if it is dropped now, and the end without a port under it is null. `target` is the port the wire is over, or null. For an end of an existing path that is moved, `detail.path` and `detail.end` are set. Use it to preview the result or to mark forbidden targets. The scene has `:state(wiring)`, a candidate port has `data-ww-port-candidate`, and the port under the pointer has `data-ww-port-over`. The pending wire is `part="link"` of the scene. A widget that draws its own cancels the `move` event, and the scene then draws none.
- **Which ports a wire has.** `endsOf(path)` returns the two ends of an attached path as `{reference, node, port, element}`, so that a click on a wire can tell which port it ends in. `wiresAt("node:port")` returns the paths that end at that port. `wiresAt("node")` returns the paths that end at the node as a whole, without those at its ports.

The example connects a source to two blocks. The source output takes two wires, and each input takes one. Wires can be taken to another input or dropped to remove them, and a click on a port starts a wire. A permission lets learners wire, and `can` refuses one port by its name. While a block moves, a readout shows where it is.

```js
import {PermissionsCore} from "@webwriter/widget/permissions"
import {SceneCore, sceneElements} from "@webwriter/widget/scene"

for (const [tag, element] of Object.entries(sceneElements)) {
  if (!customElements.get(tag)) customElements.define(tag, element)
}

class WwSignalBoard extends HTMLElement {
  static permissions = {
    allowWiring: {label: {_: "Learners may wire the blocks"}, attribute: "allow-wiring"},
  }

  #permissions = new PermissionsCore(this)
  #scene = new SceneCore(this, {
    // A connection that starts or ends at a port is asked with that port as the third argument.
    can: (action, item, port) => {
      if (action !== "connect") return true
      return this.#permissions.can("allowWiring") && port?.getAttribute("data-ww-port") !== "reserved"
    },
  })
  #places = {source: {x: 20, y: 30}, gain: {x: 240, y: 30}, sink: {x: 240, y: 130}}
  #wires = [{id: "w1", from: "source:out", to: "gain:in"}]

  constructor() {
    super()
    const root = this.attachShadow({mode: "open"})
    root.innerHTML = `
      <style>
        ww-scene { display: block; height: 220px; border: 1px solid #c8c8c8; --ww-scene-selection: #db2777; }
        ww-node { box-sizing: border-box; padding: 8px; background: white; border: 1px solid #475569; }
        .port { position: absolute; top: 20px; width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 50%; background: #16a34a; }
        .out { right: -7px; background: #2563eb; }
        .in { left: -7px; }
        .port[data-ww-port-candidate] { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #facc15; }
        .port[data-ww-port-over] { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #ea580c; }
        ww-path { stroke: #475569; stroke-width: 2px; }
        ww-path:state(rewiring) { opacity: 0.3; }
        ww-scene::part(link) { stroke: #dc2626; stroke-width: 3px; }
      </style>
      <ww-scene select="single" connect-click>
        <ww-node data-ww-key="source" width="110" height="56" selectable movable>
          Source<span class="port out" data-ww-port="out" data-ww-link="signal" data-ww-capacity="2"></span>
        </ww-node>
        <ww-node data-ww-key="gain" width="110" height="56" selectable movable>
          Gain<span class="port in" data-ww-port="in" data-ww-accept="signal" data-ww-capacity="1"></span>
        </ww-node>
        <ww-node data-ww-key="sink" width="110" height="56" selectable movable>
          Sink<span class="port in" data-ww-port="in" data-ww-accept="signal" data-ww-capacity="1"></span>
        </ww-node>
      </ww-scene>
      <output></output>
    `
    const scene = root.querySelector("ww-scene")
    scene.addEventListener("ww-move", event => this.#move(event))
    scene.addEventListener("ww-moving", event => this.#moving(event))
    scene.addEventListener("ww-connect", event => this.#connect(event))
    scene.addEventListener("ww-reconnect", event => this.#reconnect(event))
    scene.addEventListener("ww-disconnect", event => this.#disconnect(event))
    scene.addEventListener("ww-activate", event => this.#activate(event))
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#permissions.connect()
    this.#scene.connect()
    this.#render()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#scene.disconnect()
    this.#permissions.disconnect()
  }

  // Commit events change the model. The scene runs each one in an undo step together with the render.
  #move(event) {
    for (const {key, x, y} of event.detail.items) this.#places[key] = {x, y}
    this.#render()
  }

  #connect(event) {
    const {from, to} = event.detail
    this.#wires.push({id: `w${Date.now()}`, from, to})
    this.#render()
  }

  #reconnect(event) {
    const {path, from, to} = event.detail
    const wire = this.#wires.find(wire => wire.id === path.getAttribute("data-ww-key"))
    if (wire) Object.assign(wire, {from, to})
    this.#render()
  }

  #disconnect(event) {
    this.#wires = this.#wires.filter(wire => wire.id !== event.detail.path.getAttribute("data-ww-key"))
    this.#render()
  }

  // Informing events write nothing: show where the dragged block is while it moves.
  #moving(event) {
    const {state, items} = event.detail
    this.shadowRoot.querySelector("output").textContent =
      state === "move" ? items.map(item => `${item.key} ${Math.round(item.x)}, ${Math.round(item.y)}`).join("; ") : ""
  }

  #activate(event) {
    const {key, count} = event.detail
    if (count === 2) this.shadowRoot.querySelector("output").textContent = `Opened ${key}`
  }

  #render() {
    const scene = this.shadowRoot.querySelector("ww-scene")
    for (const [key, place] of Object.entries(this.#places)) {
      const node = scene.querySelector(`ww-node[data-ww-key="${key}"]`)
      node.setAttribute("x", String(place.x))
      node.setAttribute("y", String(place.y))
    }
    const ids = new Set(this.#wires.map(wire => wire.id))
    for (const path of scene.querySelectorAll("ww-path")) {
      if (!ids.has(path.getAttribute("data-ww-key"))) path.remove()
    }
    for (const wire of this.#wires) {
      let path = scene.querySelector(`ww-path[data-ww-key="${wire.id}"]`)
      if (!path) {
        path = document.createElement("ww-path")
        path.setAttribute("data-ww-key", wire.id)
        path.setAttribute("route", "orthogonal")
        path.setAttribute("marker-end", "arrow")
        path.setAttribute("rewire", "from to")
        path.setAttribute("hit-width", "20")
        path.toggleAttribute("selectable", true)
        scene.prepend(path)
      }
      path.setAttribute("from", wire.from)
      path.setAttribute("to", wire.to)
    }
    this.#scene.refresh()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-signal-board", WwSignalBoard)
```

#### Constraints

Constraints are attributes of the item, read while it is moved or resized, by pointer and by keyboard. The preview obeys them.

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `axis="x"` or `axis="y"` | The item moves along that axis only. |
| `min-x`, `max-x`, `min-y`, `max-y` | The `x` and `y` of the item stay between these. |
| `bounds="x y width height"` | The whole box of the item stays inside this box, when it moves and when an edge is dragged. |
| `grid` | A snap grid of the item itself, instead of the scene's. |
| `resizable` | Handles of the selected item: all eight without a value, or the ones named, as in `resizable="s"` or `resizable="e w"`. `n`, `e`, `s`, and `w` are the edges, and `ne`, `se`, `sw`, and `nw` the corners. For a node, a rect, and an image. |
| `min-width`, `min-height`, `max-width`, `max-height` | The size limits of a resize. The edge that is dragged stops. A node has a minimum of 16 without them. |
| `keep-ratio` | A node keeps its proportions while it is resized. |

Several items that move together keep every limit of every item. A key that is pressed against a limit does not go on counting. The handles of a rect and an image are in the scene's own tree, and as large on the screen at any zoom. A rect that is turned has none. The scene attribute `move-step` sets the step of the arrow keys. Limits apply to items that are `movable`. A member of a group that moves follows the group.

The example moves a task bar along one axis in steps of 20 and resizes it by its side edges, and keeps a marker inside a band. The widget keeps the committed geometry in the attributes of the items.

```js
import {SceneCore, sceneElements} from "@webwriter/widget/scene"

for (const [tag, element] of Object.entries(sceneElements)) {
  if (!customElements.get(tag)) customElements.define(tag, element)
}

class WwSchedule extends HTMLElement {
  #scene = new SceneCore(this)

  constructor() {
    super()
    const root = this.attachShadow({mode: "open"})
    root.innerHTML = `
      <style>
        ww-scene { display: block; height: 160px; border: 1px solid #c8c8c8; }
        ww-node { box-sizing: border-box; background: #dbeafe; border: 1px solid #2563eb; }
        ww-shape { fill: #fde68a; stroke: #b45309; }
      </style>
      <ww-scene select="single" move-step="10">
        <ww-node data-ww-key="task" x="40" y="20" width="120" height="32"
                 axis="x" min-x="0" max-x="400" grid="20"
                 resizable="e w" min-width="40" max-width="240" selectable movable>Build</ww-node>
        <ww-shape data-ww-key="marker" kind="rect" x="40" y="80" width="24" height="40"
                  bounds="0 70 400 80" resizable="n s" min-height="20" selectable movable></ww-shape>
      </ww-scene>
    `
    const scene = root.querySelector("ww-scene")
    scene.addEventListener("ww-move", event => this.#move(event))
    scene.addEventListener("ww-resize", event => this.#resize(event))
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#scene.connect()
    this.#scene.refresh()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#scene.disconnect()
  }

  #move(event) {
    for (const {key, x, y} of event.detail.items) {
      const item = this.shadowRoot.querySelector(`[data-ww-key="${key}"]`)
      item.setAttribute("x", String(x))
      item.setAttribute("y", String(y))
    }
  }

  #resize(event) {
    const {item, x, y, width, height} = event.detail
    for (const [name, value] of Object.entries({x, y, width, height})) item.setAttribute(name, String(value))
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-schedule", WwSchedule)
```

#### Hit testing

`itemAt(point)` returns the topmost item at a point, or null for the background. `itemsAt(point)` returns all items there, the topmost first. The point is in scene coordinates, or in client coordinates with `{client: true}`. `toScene(clientX, clientY)` and `toClient(x, y)` convert between the two through the view.

The answer comes from geometry and works for any point, also where no pointer is. A node counts inside its outline, a path in its hit band and on its markers and labels, and a shape, a text, or an image anywhere inside it, filled or not. A group counts only in its frame. Nodes are above everything that is drawn, and drawn items count from the last in the template to the first. An item with `pointer-events: none` is left out.

### Print note

The print note is a short text that is shown on paper only, for a widget without a print view: it tells the reader to open the document online and shows the address of the document where it is known. `PrintNoteCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/print`; the bindings are `PrintNote`, `usePrintNote`, `usePrintNote`, `printNoteStore`, and `injectPrintNote`. See [Print note](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#print-note).

The core has `text` and `address` in its snapshot. It adds `<p data-ww-print-note>` at the end of the shadow root, or fills the one that the template has, and removes it when the widget disconnects. The options are `address`, `messages`, and `root`. `documentAddress()` is exported with the core.

```js
import {PrintNoteCore} from "@webwriter/widget/print"

class WwSimulation extends HTMLElement {
  #note = new PrintNoteCore(this)

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `<slot></slot><p data-ww-print-note></p>`
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#note.connect()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#note.disconnect()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-simulation", WwSimulation)
```

### Playback

Playback holds the run state of a widget that plays over time, with the interface of a media element. `PlaybackCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/playback`; the bindings are `usePlayback`, `usePlayback`, `playbackStore`, and `injectPlayback`.

Configure the run with `step`, with `steps` and `show`, with `play` and `pause`, or with `media`. Mark buttons with `data-ww-playback="toggle"`, `play`, `pause`, `step`, `back`, `reset`, or `rate`, a range input with `seek`, and an `<output>` with `time`. The event is `ww-playbackchange`. See [Playback](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#playback).

```js
import {PlaybackCore} from "@webwriter/widget/playback"

const STEPS = ["Boil the water", "Add the pasta", "Drain and serve"]

class WwRecipe extends HTMLElement {
  #playback = new PlaybackCore(this, {
    steps: () => STEPS.length,
    show: index => (this.shadowRoot.querySelector("p").textContent = STEPS[index]),
    interval: 3,
  })

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `
      <p>${STEPS[0]}</p>
      <button data-ww-playback="back"></button>
      <button data-ww-playback="toggle"></button>
      <button data-ww-playback="step"></button>
      <input type="range" data-ww-playback="seek">
      <output data-ww-playback="time"></output>
    `
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#playback.connect()
    this.#playback.refresh()
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.#playback.disconnect()
  }
}

customElements.define("ww-recipe", WwRecipe)
```

### Data block (`jsonData`)

The data block helper gives typed access to the widget's JSON [data block](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/data.md). `JsonDataCore` is in `@webwriter/widget/data` and needs a host with `widgetRuntime`, which `withWidgetRuntime` adds. The bindings are `useJsonData`, `useJsonData`, `jsonDataStore`, and `injectJsonData`.

`defaults` gives the value for keys that the block lacks. `get()` reads the value, `set(partial)` changes it, and the event `ww-dataerror` reports a snapshot that the helper could not use. See [Data block](../domeditor/docs/widgets/reference/lit.md#data-block-jsondata).

```js
import {withWidgetRuntime} from "@webwriter/widget"
import {JsonDataCore} from "@webwriter/widget/data"

class WwTally extends withWidgetRuntime(HTMLElement) {
  #data = new JsonDataCore(this, {
    defaults: {count: 0},
    validate: ({count}) => Number.isInteger(count) && count >= 0,
  })
  #unsubscribe

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.attachShadow({mode: "open"}).innerHTML = `<button></button>`
    this.shadowRoot.querySelector("button").addEventListener("click", () => this.#data.set({count: this.#data.get().count + 1}))
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    super.connectedCallback()
    this.#data.connect()
    this.#unsubscribe = this.#data.subscribe(() => this.#render())
```
